I like the game a lot but I can understand some of the issues people have:

It runs like shit on consoles and some PCs. (runs fine for me but I upgraded just to play this)

They ruined the conversation system. That's all there is to it. They made it EXACTLY like Mass Effect and I don't think anyone wanted that.

They did away with the skill system. Skills were always part of the experience and personally I miss them. Now there are hard level limits on what areas you can access (ie, you can not unlock Master level locks or terminals until the level that perk is available), this was never the case before. If you wanted to put all your points into Lockpick for the first ten levels and access shit you 'shouldn't' that was up to you.

They fucked with power armor. I don't like that either, but I can deal... mainly by stockpiling fusion cores till the endgame and getting the perk that doubles their duration.

The town building 'minigame' is not everyone's cup of tea. It doesn't bother me but I understand the lashback, it's Fallout not Minecraft or the Sims.

I felt the shooting was a huge upgrade over the last 2 games but part of the reason for that is your ability to hit shit is no longer skill % based, it's all personal skill and weapon accuracy. This doesn't bother me either but it does make the game feel significantly easier at low level. I'm level 13, with level 1 armor and gun mod perks, all my weapons and armor are as modded as possible (metal and leather, 10mm pistols, combat shotgun, combat rifle, minigun, sniper rifle) and I feel pretty fucking OP against anything thats not in power armor.

Some people don't like the new aesthetic; personally I like it a lot. Look at the graphics for FO3/NV, the models are fucking ugly as shit.

Only 1 companion now? Lame. I can't have a dude follow me AND a dog? What am I fucking autistic?

The crafting system is really tied into the main game and I guess not everyone likes that? That's probably my favorite part of the game, that I am justified in picking through all the shit from prewar, looking for stupid things like desk fans and board games and pottery.

Now, I avoid the hype train, I don't even watch trailers anymore let alone follow preview info and first looks or whatever. And I'm pretty annoyed by the new conversation system; dialogs were always one of my absolutely favorite parts of the Fallout experience, going back to when I played the first in 97. The NPCs are a really mixed bag, I've only met a couple I even remember and their backstories are mostly implied because I can't talk to them about more than 2 or 3 topics. A lot of the NPCs I want to kill (and hopefully will, later). But despite all this, the game is a lot of fun and I can't wait to get out of work to play it more. I have 26 hrs logged already since Tuesday and I've worked everyday. It is imperfect and has clear flaws but it is the best AAA game this year other than MGSV. tbh imo fam
